Subject: Redwood — detailed assurance artifacts for RFP section 4.2

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we finalize the RFP response for Harbor Health EU, procurement has asked for a more detailed breakdown of Redwood's assurance controls against both the NIST AI RMF and the EU AI Act (for high-risk systems). Specifically they want:

- a capability mapping (controls -> RMF subcategories + EU obligations)
- examples of artifacts we can share (document samples, tests, code snippets)
- the eval/regression approach you use to detect model degradation and how you sample for manual review
- retention and audit log practices for traceability and human oversight evidence

Can you provide a short deliverable (PDF + spreadsheet) and a 30–40 minute technical deep-dive next week? Procurement would like these materials attached to the final bid by 24 Mar.

Best,
Elena

Elena — thanks for the clear ask. We're aligned on the deliverables and can get a concise package over to you ahead of your procurement deadline. Quick summary of what we'll send and a proposed plan: 

Deliverables (attached):
- Redwood_NIST_RMF_mapping_v1.pdf — control-level mapping to NIST AI RMF and the EU AI Act with implementation notes
- eu-ai-act-mitigation-matrix.xlsx — risk/mitigation matrix you can drop into your compliance spreadsheet
- eval-regression-harness-snippet.md — short code + config snippets showing our sampling, metrics, and rollback triggers

What you'll see in the package (high level):
- Governance & documentation: model inventory, model card templates, decision logs, and DPIA checklist for EU deployments
- Evaluation & regression: continuous eval harness (automated metric checks + periodic manual sampling), regression sampling by stratified prompt buckets, and canary rollouts for model updates
- Monitoring & traceability: production logging (per-request trace id, prompt/response hashes, model_version), retention policy options (30/90/365 days), and audit export templates for third-party review
- EU AI Act specifics: documentation for high-risk classification, human oversight design, transparency statements, and rights-to-explanation artifacts; plus guidance for data minimization and DPIA evidence

Proposed timeline:
- Today: draft materials (we've attached v1 artifacts)
- Tue/Wed (23–24 Mar): 30–40 min tech deep-dive with our applied ML + security reps
- By 24 Mar EOD: final PDF + spreadsheet for your procurement bundle

Next steps: tell me a few slots that work for your team for the deep-dive. We'll include Monica (legal/compliance) and Karthik (inference lead) on the call.

Attachments: Redwood_NIST_RMF_mapping_v1.pdf, eu-ai-act-mitigation-matrix.xlsx, eval-regression-harness-snippet.md

Thanks — Aditya

Elena / Aditya — looping in a few clarifications from Legal & CS so we can make the package procurement-ready. Two asks from our side: 

1) Retention & exports: Harbor Health, can you confirm the target retention window you prefer for per-request payloads and logs? Our standard options are 30 / 90 / 365 days — if you need something custom we can scope it as part of the procurement addendum.

2) Evidence types: procurement often asks for living evidence (e.g., screenshots of the SOC2 portal + sample CSV export). We can include redacted examples, but to avoid shipping PII we will provide synthetic samples and a pointer to where Harbor reviewers can pull full audit exports under an NDA.

Operational notes we'll include in the guide:
- Regression sampling cadence: weekly automated checks + monthly stratified manual review (unless you request an accelerated cadence)
- Canary policy example: 10% traffic canary for 48–72 hours with automatic rollback on metric regressions
- Incident trace template and how it maps to SIEM ingestion endpoints (we use structured JSON logs with trace IDs)

I'll be on the deep-dive. If procurement prefers, we can supply a short contractual clause for audit rights and data handling for EU deployments.

Monica Patel
VP, Customer Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
